correctness.rationale: The outer cut indicators p have no adjacent ones and force the spoke discrepancy s_i=1-p_(i-1)-p_i. Substituting b_i=a_i XOR s_i in b_i XOR b_(i+2) cancels the interior p terms and gives p_(i-1) XOR p_(i+2). The inner equation forces p_(i-3)=p_(i+2) for each admissible adjacent pair: if both p's are zero, both outer bits must also be zero; otherwise the inner equation reduces to equality of those outer bits. Thus p has period five; when 5 does not divide n, gcd(n,5)=1 forces p=0. On a five-cycle a singleton 1 violates the zero-pair rule; the five rotations of (1,0,1,0,0) each meet it (the only adjacent zero pair is between its two trailing zeros). The empty and two-one patterns have even parity, so integration around the ring closes and leaves only a global colour flip. Reconstruction gives the stated template up to shift and complement, also at n=5. For a connected graph the crossing-edge indicators determine all colours once one vertex colour is fixed. Thus the cut enumeration is precisely half the labelled count.
residual_risks: The direct check only covers the listed finite orders; the period argument and closed-walk characterization are all-order.
